chunks: And Zurarah said: I said to Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, “Tell me, when the deceased dies, why is the palm branch placed with him?” So he said:

“The punishment and the accounting are kept away from him so long as the stick remains fresh. The accounting and punishment altogether are only in one day, in one moment, equal to the time in which he is placed in the grave and the people return. The two palm branches were only placed for that reason, so no punishment and no accounting will afflict him after they have dried, if Allah, Exalted is He, wills.”

key_terms.السَّعَفَتَانِ: the two palm branches used for this purpose
key_terms.الْجَرِيدَةُ: the palm branch placed with the deceased
key_terms.الْحِسَابُ: the reckoning or accounting faced by the deceased
key_terms.الْعَذَابُ: punishment affecting the deceased after burial
key_terms.الْقَبْرَ: the grave into which the deceased is placed
key_terms.جُفُوفِهِمَا: the drying of the two branches

ai.seo_question: Why is a palm branch placed with the deceased in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the reason for placing palm branches with the deceased: they serve as a means by which punishment and reckoning are averted during the initial period after burial. It reflects a teaching about the state of the deceased in the grave and the wisdom of a funerary practice transmitted from the Imams عليهم السلام.
